title: 2021 Fall AMC 10A Problem 14
statement: How many ordered pairs \((x,y)\) of real numbers satisfy the following system of equations? \[\begin{aligned} x^2+3y&=9, \\ (|x|+|y|-4)^2&=1. \end{aligned}\]

solutions.text:
Put \(t=|x|.\) The second equation gives \(t+|y|=3\) or \(5,\) while the first gives \(y=3-\frac{t^2}{3}.\)

If \(y\ge0,\) then \(0\le t\le3.\) For \(t+y=3,\) substitution gives \(t-\frac{t^2}{3}=0,\) so \(t=0\) or \(3.\) These yield \(x=0,3,-3,\) for three points. For \(t+y=5,\) substitution gives \(t^2-3t+6=0,\) which has no real root.

If \(y<0,\) then \(t>3.\) The equation \(t-y=3\) gives \(t^2+3t-18=0,\) whose only nonnegative root is the excluded boundary value \(t=3.\) The equation \(t-y=5\) gives \(t^2+3t-24=0,\) with exactly one positive root \(t=\frac{-3+\sqrt{105}}2>3.\) It yields two points, one for each sign of \(x.\)

The total number of ordered pairs is \(3+2=5.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Use \(y=3-\frac{x^2}{3}\) and check the sign ranges for \(x,y\)
